page_title: Cloud services: what they are and what they cost
title: Cloud services: what they are and what they cost
standfirst: An index of {types} service types, the {units} units they are measured in, and {offers} specific offers verified against each provider's documentation. Built to answer the same eight questions every time, so you can compare apples to apples.
how_1: Types and units barely change; prices do, and fast. That is why they are kept apart: every offer carries its own date and source.
how_2: Before comparing two offers, look at the unit. “10 ms of CPU per request” and “180,000 vCPU-seconds per month” are not the same quantity, and mixing them up leads to a bad choice.
how_3: Tell a pool from a cap. A monthly pool you can spend however you like; a per-request cap makes every expensive operation fail, even when the month is untouched.
how_4: The data lives in data/*.json. node scripts/validate.mjs flags anything left unverified for more than 90 days.
offers_desc: Each card answers the eight questions. Anything marked “secondary source” could not be confirmed in the provider's official documentation: confirm it before deciding.
types_desc: What each thing is, what it is for, what it is measured in, and which pitfalls come with it.
units_title: How things are measured and billed
units_desc: The vocabulary that makes offers comparable. Each unit is explained first precisely and then in plain words.
limits_desc: Before the units, this: the same figure means very different things depending on how it is applied.
footer: Generated from data/*.json and locales/ with node scripts/build.mjs. Do not edit by hand: change the data and regenerate. The complete data is embedded in this page as JSON under the ids guide-data (English) and guide-data-es (Spanish), so it can be extracted programmatically.
